prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: The appraisal report's actual numbers: (1) the appraised value of the 8.5-acre property valued as a permitted concrete-batch-plant site (its 'existing use' value under the Ocean Concrete holding), and (2) the appraised value of the same property under the current zoning that excludes batch plants. The difference between those two figures is the diminution-in-value measure of Bert Harris Act compensation. Also useful: any specific dollar demand the landowner has made to the County post-remand, the landowner's own stated opinion of value if different from the appraisal, and documentation of the costs he sunk into site preparation (wells, clearing, tree relocation) if those are being claimed as a separate component of loss.
prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability is already decided in the landowner's favor by a published appellate opinion, and the County enters the damages trial with no valuation experts after the court excluded both of its witnesses — a strongly favorable posture for a meaningful compensation award under the Bert Harris Act's 'existing use' valuation standard. The ultimate dollar result will turn heavily on the jury's acceptance of the landowner's appraisal and personal valuation testimony, which is now largely unrebutted by competing expert opinion, but the actual figures are not present in the materials provided, so no dollar range can be computed from this record alone.

outcome.description: At a four-day jury trial in September 2019, with the County's economist and appraiser excluded, the jury awarded the landowner $2 million; final judgment was entered for $2 million plus $1,302,577 in prejudgment interest. The Fourth District affirmed on November 25, 2020. Amount used excludes prejudgment interest.
